claim: Think-SFT's own ChatML <think> template does not make it drift less: on hard328 at cap 32,768, the share of rows whose first 16,384 tokens contain a drift sign (switch into a non-Latin script or a repeated 50-token window) is the same as with the raw template and the cue. Only where the final answer is stated changes.
why_only_this: run-04/f2-m05 is the only other mechanism that talks about the template, and it predicts the opposite: in its own format Think-SFT samples a sharper, on-distribution distribution, so fewer long answers drift, while raw-template cue runs keep the drift. That mechanism needs native drift to be clearly lower; this one needs it unchanged, because the template only sets where the answer is stated and the model reasons as well either way. The rest say nothing about Think-SFT's template. They cover the RL direction split (round-10/weights-m06), how capped rows are rescored (run-08/f2-m02, round-09/grader-m06), seed scatter (round-09/grader-m01, run-08/f2-m01), cap-hit abstention in votes (run-08/f2-m06), the difficulty mix (round-09/grader-m04) and the stratum split of edits (round-10/problems-m04). None of them predicts any template effect on drift, in either direction.
computation: 1. Load the per-problem rows of the native cell (studies/rlneurons/results/native/hard328-01: Think-SFT, own chat format, cap 32,768; result-dd9239, 232 at 32k, 204 at 16k). Load the matched raw-template cue cell at the same cap (studies/rlneurons/results/cap32/sft_cue-01; its text rows are in cap32/rows-01 or rows-02, whichever holds the sft_cue rows: 230 at 32k, 207 at 16k, result-c8b994). Join the two on problem index, giving 328 pairs. Before going on, check that each cell's v3-right count matches its posted 32k and 16k count. 2. Cut every row to its first 16,384 generated tokens. Use the stored token ids if the rows have them. Otherwise tokenize the text offline with the Think-SFT tokenizer (allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Think-SFT), on CPU. Comparing at a common length means the native cell's longer answers cannot add drift chances. 3. On each cut row, compute the two drift signs exactly as analysis/drift.py defines them (the same code that produced studies/rlneurons/results/drift/describe-01): (a) the first token position where the text switches into a non-Latin script (CJK, Cyrillic and the rest, per drift.py's script rule); (b) the first position where a 50-token window repeats an earlier window. A row is drifted if (a) or (b) fires anywhere in the first 16,384 tokens. Before running, reproduce drift.py's planted tests (analysis/drift_test.py) and check that the raw-cue drift rate you get on thinkvote sample 0 matches describe-01's stored value for the same rows. 4. Primary statistic: D = (drifted share, native) - (drifted share, raw cue at cap 32k), in percentage points of 328. Get a 95 % interval by a paired bootstrap over problems (10,000 resamples, seed 0). 5. Null: the seed scatter of the same quantity within the raw-cue template. Take the four raw-cue samples in studies/rlneurons/results/thinkvote/hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01 (cap 16,384, so their rows already end at 16,384 tokens), compute each sample's drifted share with the same code, and report every pairwise difference and the largest one in absolute value, S_max. Also compute D against each of the four thinkvote samples, cutting the native rows to 16,384 tokens as in step 2. 6. Secondary checks, reported but not deciding: (i) cap hits at 16,384 and median tokens of finished rows, native against raw cue, which this mechanism says are unchanged; (ii) on the raw-cue rows that v3 grades wrong and that finished, the number whose next non-empty line after the last line reading 'Answer:' (case-insensitive, markdown stripped, nothing after the colon) is math-verify-equivalent to the gold answer. This mechanism says these are the only rows the native template recovers. 7. Report D with its interval, S_max, the four D values against the thinkvote samples, and the secondary numbers.
refuted_if: The native template drifts clearly less than the raw template with the cue: D is at most -2.0 points (about 7 of 328 rows fewer drifted), the upper end of its paired 95 % interval is below 0, and |D| is larger than S_max, the largest drift-share difference between two raw-cue samples.
threshold: D <= -2.0 percentage points of 328, with paired-bootstrap 95 % upper bound < 0 and |D| > S_max. If any of these fails, the claim holds. If D comes out positive, that also counts against f2-m05.
null: Seed scatter within one template. The drift-share differences between the four stored raw-cue samples (thinkvote hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01) set how large a template difference has to be to count. This is stronger than a random baseline: it is the same model, prompt and grader on a second base sample, so any native-minus-raw difference inside S_max is indistinguishable from re-sampling.
